title: Type look: subtle idle motion that makes it feel alive
description:
Add 3 subtle always-on motions to the Type look, inside the RD-02 policy, so it feels alive while open. The maintainer wants calm, not flashy.

Do:
- Caret breathes: opacity 0.6 to 1.0 on a 2 s cycle, in its own box after the last word; it never moves the text.
- Baseline grid pulses with the level: grid alpha 4 % at rest, up to 7 % with the smoothed level.
- Ink sheen: once every 12 s a 1 s sheen crosses the status word. (The plan said the last word; that is on the reading line, so it moves to the status word.)
- Run through the RD-02 paced idle path at its capped rate, only while the popup is open; stop at once on exit and on a look switch. Nothing changes the glyphs of the newest line.
- Reduced motion (`reduced-motion` or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1): all of them off, the look still.
Files: src/bin/osd_vo/type_look.rs.

Acceptance (B = target/release/voxtype-osd-vo built through heavy-build with `--features osd-vo`; D = a new empty folder):
- Given type open with no speech, when the RD-02 per-look measurement runs, then idle frames stay at or under the capped rate. CPU and GPU stay under the RD-02 budget (proposed: 2 % of one core, 1 ms GPU per frame at 600x300).
- Given `B --theme type --offline D --moment long-silence`, when two idle-tail frames 1 s apart are compared (`compare -metric AE`), then some panel pixels differ and none inside the newest line's box (newest_line_centre +/- half a line).
- Given the same run with VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, then those two frames are identical.
- Given done and cancel (`--offline D --cancel`), then the run exits 0 and no "still moving" in stderr.
- Given the look chord steps away while idle, then the old idle loops stop in that frame.
- `B --theme type --envelope` adds no breach with the idle motion on.
Tests: the checks above; the RD-02 number for this look goes in docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md.

title: R2-15 Bioluminescent: Breathing Membrane, Prism Light, Ink Reveal
description:
Why: Biolume is a glowing bubble with tendrils. Round 2 makes it breathe, catch light and leave ink around the words. Design: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/redesign2/15.png.

Do:
- Breathing Membrane (R2-15-a):
  - What: three layered closed paths with noise wobble grow with the voice; tendrils sway.
  - Driver and place: smoothed RMS. Around the bubble and text; tendrils stay inside the popup.
  - Subtle: layer alpha 20 % or less. Reduced: still membranes.
  - Uses: paths; EG-13 for the tendrils.
- Prism Light (R2-15-b):
  - What: soft god rays through the bubble and a rim hue band with a few glints; fades out over 600 ms on finish.
  - Driver and place: RMS for brightness. Bubble rim, not over the newest line.
  - Subtle: ray alpha 12 % or less. Reduced: still hue band.
  - Uses: gradient cones or vo-3d light cones; no EG.
- Ink Reveal (R2-15-c):
  - What: ink clouds swirl around and behind the text, fed at the newest word's box; wisps drift away.
  - Driver and place: word-commit and RMS. Behind the text; ink alpha at the newest line 20 % or less.
  - Subtle: one hue. Reduced: still ink wash.
  - Uses: EG-11, EG-12.

Files: the biolume look file RD-03 creates in ~/work/voxtype/src/bin/osd_vo/; exhibits station/r2_15_a_breathing_membrane.rs, r2_15_b_prism_light.rs and r2_15_c_ink_reveal.rs.

- Given `--theme biolume --offline DIR --moment M` for first-word, dictation, pause and final-pass, then dictation shows large membranes and rays; first-word +0.3 s shows ink at the word; final-pass +0.6 s shows no rays.
- Given the same script, when `--envelope` runs, then it passes (newest line: ink 70 % or more, baseline within 3 px, no scale, rotation or blur).
- Given idle-open and recording, then the RD-02 log shows idle at 30 fps or less, CPU under 2 % of a core, GPU p95 under 1 ms at 600x300.
- Given a full dictation and a cancel, then the RD-05 exit check passes.
- Given `--station --only R2-15-a,R2-15-b,R2-15-c`, then each idea plays alone in its own tile.
- Given `--motion reduced-motion`, then the moments show each reduced form above.
- Human check: the maintainer approves a recorded clip of one dictation (`--record`, played with `--preview --replay`).

title: EG-08 Effects can leave the popup: automatic margins and a fly-out layer
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 2.

Why: glows and motion get cut at the surface edge. vo already sizes a transparent margin from `Scene::effect_reach` (`SurfaceMargin::Auto`, crates/vo/src/lib.rs), but only from the first view (crates/vo/src/live.rs, `start_inner`), so an effect that starts later, such as an exit streak, is clipped. Big exits (a text card flying to the app, long streaks, a reflection below the popup) also need room far outside the popup.

Do:
- Margins that follow the show: when a later view reaches further than the current margin, grow the surface (mid-show resize exists) without moving the panel on screen; shrink back once the effect settles. Keep a small hysteresis so the surface does not resize every frame. The margin never shrinks below the first view's.
- A fly-out layer: an element can ask to draw on a short-lived full-screen click-through surface (`InputMode::None`, on the popup's output) for big exits. It opens when the element needs it and closes when the element settles or at the exit cap (EXIT_MOTION_MAX), whichever is first. It uses the existing multi-surface support (crates/vo/src/surfaces.rs; the popup's captions look uses several surfaces).
- Reduced motion: a fly-out element ends in place (fade), so no fly-out surface opens.
- In the popup, switch one look (swiss) from its hand-set surface size to the automatic margin as the example. Other looks adopt it in their own beads.
Files: crates/vo/src/live.rs, crates/vo/src/surfaces.rs, crates/vo-scene/src/reach.rs; src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs (swiss `surface()` only) in the popup.

Acceptance:
- Given a vo test app whose view adds a glow of radius 40 px at t = 1 s, when its driver runs (unit test, no display), then `Scene::clipped` is zero at every frame, and the main surface is larger only while the glow shows.
- Given an exit card that flies 800 px up, then a fly-out surface opens, the card is never clipped (`clipped` zero on that surface), and the surface closes within EXIT_MOTION_MAX of the exit.
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, then no fly-out surface opens.
- Given the popup idle with no effect showing, then its surface size equals the first view's size (logged), and no extra surface is open.
- Given swiss, when `voxtype-osd-vo --envelope --theme swiss` runs, then it exits 0, and `--exit-check --theme swiss` (RD-05, if landed) exits 0.
Tests: vo unit tests for grow, shrink, hysteresis and fly-out open and close; a vo example of the fly-out in a nested `kwin_wayland --virtual` with surface sizes logged; `just test`, `just test-gpu`, `just budget` exit 0.

title: EG-01 Backdrop capture: render the layers under an element into a texture
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 3, 4, 5, 11.

Why: ripples that bend (EG-03), refracting glass (EG-05), layer blur and frost (EG-04), water reflections (EG-10) and text on surfaces all need the pixels under an element. Today no element can read what was drawn before it.

Do:
- An element or layer can ask for a backdrop: everything drawn before it in the same surface, rendered into an offscreen texture at full or half resolution, and handed to its draw (to the renderer side that EG-02, EG-03 and EG-04 will use).
- Reuse the effect path's offscreen targets and texture pool (crates/vo-render/src/offscreen.rs, renderer/compose.rs). Allocate and copy nothing when no element asks.
- The display list carries the request (a flag in crates/vo-scene/src/display.rs) and an element API in crates/vo-scene/src/element.rs. The backdrop is in physical pixels, so fractional scales (1.25, 1.5) sample without drift.
- Never reads the desktop: a backdrop holds only this surface's own drawing (decision: no screen capture).
- Add a case `backdrop` (full and half) to crates/vo/examples/effect_cost.rs.
Files: crates/vo-render/src/renderer.rs, renderer/compose.rs, offscreen.rs; crates/vo-scene/src/display.rs, element.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a test scene (a striped panel, then an element that draws its backdrop tinted red), when rendered offscreen, then it matches a new golden in crates/vo-render/tests/gpu_backdrop.rs; the same at scale 1.5.
- Given half resolution, then the golden matches within the golden tolerance and the texture is a quarter of the pixels.
- Given any scene that asks for no backdrop, then every existing golden is unchanged (`just test-gpu` passes without `just golden-update`) and pooled texture memory in the effect_cost table is unchanged for those cases.
- Given effect_cost at 600x300, then `backdrop` adds under VO_BUDGET_EFFECT_MS (2 ms) and the number is in the commit message.
- Given two renders of the same scene at the same t, then they are byte-identical.

title: RD-01 Each look turns on its own motion set by default
description:
Why: the everyday popup shows almost none of the 73 motion exhibits. Features turn on only through `--motion` or VOXTYPE_OSD_VO_MOTION, and the daemon passes neither. This bead gives each look a default motion set, so each look runs the effects its redesign chose.

Do:
- New src/bin/osd_vo/defaults.rs with `pub(crate) fn defaults(theme: OsdTheme) -> &'static [&'static str]`. Fill the rows of the 20 existing looks from docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 3 (backticked names only; built-in effects need no entry). End the match with `_ => &[]`, so the 7 new looks (RD-03) need no edit here; each new look's FX bead adds its own row.
- `Look::on` (src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs) also answers true for `defaults(self.theme)`, unless the resolved motion setting is `none`. Read `self.theme` at call time, never a list resolved at startup, so a look switch with the look chord mid-show uses the new look's set.
- Config `[osd] motion` in src/osd/config.rs: `"look"` (default, the look's set), `"none"` (no defaults, today's behaviour), or a list of names. A list with any plain name replaces the set; `no-<name>` removes a name; a list of only `no-` entries means the look's set minus those. CLI `--motion` and VOXTYPE_OSD_VO_MOTION win over the config and follow the same rules (`--motion none` works). Missing field = `"look"`; an unknown name is ignored, never an error.
- Station exhibits (`--station`) keep exactly their own features, as if motion were `none`, so each exhibit still shows one effect. `--wall`, `--offline` and `--envelope` use the look's set.
- `reduced-motion` (feature or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1) leaves the set on; each effect draws its reduced form as today.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: document `[osd] motion` next to `look_chord`, with the per-look sets and the opt-out.

title: EG-32 Liquid morph in the live text
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 18.

Why: the liquid morph (`glyph_fx::Effect::Morph`, crates/vo-3d/src/glyph_fx.rs) only runs as a separate GPU element the app places by hand (src/bin/osd_vo/letter_fx.rs), in flat colour. It should be a live-text revision motion like the palimpsest.

- flow.rs: `Revise::Liquid`. For a revised word it emits a GPU item whose source is plain data defined in vo-scene (`LiquidRevision`: old and new glyphs, positions from the flow's springs, start time, ink, material id) and hides the word's own glyphs for the morph (at most 400 ms).
- glyph_fx.rs: the Morph painter also draws `LiquidRevision` (`glyph_fx::install` registers it). Without the painter, `Revise::Liquid` falls back to `Palimpsest` and logs once at debug.
- On the reading line, kept letters stay solid and new letters are drawn at ink 0.7 or more from their first frame; the liquid is the old letters draining plus colour around the new. Older lines get the full fill.

- Reduced motion: the corrected word at once.
- Popup: station exhibit `liquid-revise`.

- Given a revision, then kept letters' positions change by at most their spring step per frame (no jump), and the morph ends within 400 ms.
- Given no painter installed, then the result equals `Revise::Palimpsest` (display-list equality).
- Two `--offline` renders are byte-identical; `--gpu-times` p95 at most 1 ms at 600x300, logged.

title: EG-15 Per-glyph transforms in the text renderer
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 8.

Why: rotating letters today need one layer per glyph. Thousands of letters should move on their own in one draw.

Do:
- Add `xform: GlyphXform { rot_deg, skew_deg, offset: Point }` to `vo_scene::display::GlyphInstance`, pivot at the centre of the glyph's ink box, `GlyphXform::IDENTITY` as default.
- Fold it into the Slug instance's `lin` (2x2 em-to-pixel matrix) and `offset` in crates/vo-render/src/text/slug_gpu.rs. The matrix is already general, so prefer CPU-only; change slug-glyph.wgsl only if the quad or the effects (blur, wipe, halo offset) assume no rotation.
- `Painter::glyph` and live-text motions get it through the struct.
- cpu.rs (CPU first frame): apply the same transform to the outline fill.
- envelope.rs: the tracker reads `xform`: rotation counts against `rotation_deg`; add `skew_deg` (default 5, the `READING_SLNT` range in var_axes.rs).
- Update every `GlyphInstance {` literal (about 24 files in both repos, `grep -rln "GlyphInstance {"`) with `xform: GlyphXform::IDENTITY`. Mechanical.
- Demo: a case in crates/vo/examples/effect_cost.rs plus a page in type_demo.

title: EG-03 Displacement pass: ripples, noise and curls bend a layer
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 3.

Why: the only distortions today are CRT curvature, glitch slices, chromatic split, perspective warp and motion blur. Sonic ripples, liquid echoes and ink smears need a layer redrawn with each pixel moved by a field.

Do:
- A displacement pass: redraw a captured layer (EG-01) with each pixel offset by a source. Sources: expanding ripple rings seeded by events (closed form in t, so they replay), noise and curl fields (the existing WGSL noise), a page-curl cylinder, and a texture of offsets (any texture; EG-10 later feeds it water heights, this bead tests it with a synthetic texture).
- API on elements or layers, for example `Element::displace(Displace::Ripples { .. })`; strength animatable and bindable to a signal.
- The newest (reading) line is exempt by default: a mask keeps it sharp and still, so the reading-line envelope holds. An explicit opt-out exists for text that is not read.
- Reduced motion: displacement strength 0 (the layer draws as captured, no pass cost).
- Add effect_cost cases `displace ripples` and `displace noise`.
Files: crates/vo-render/src/displace.rs and wgsl/displace.wgsl (new); crates/vo-scene/src/element.rs, display.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a demo with a waveform and an older text line under two ripple rings from onsets at t = 0.2 and 0.5 s, when rendered offscreen at t = 0.8 s, then it matches a new golden in crates/vo-render/tests/gpu_displace.rs, and the reading line's pixels equal the same scene without displacement.
- Given the texture source with a constant offset of (3, 0) px, then the output equals the input shifted 3 px (within golden tolerance).
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1 or strength 0, then output equals the undisplaced layer, byte for byte.
- Given the same demo rendered twice, and once with a seek back from t = 1.5 s to 0.8 s, then frames at equal t are byte-identical.
- Given each other source (noise, curl, page curl) on the same layer, then each matches its own golden.
- Given the demo through `vo::envelope::check_scenario`, then it passes.
- Given effect_cost at 600x300, then each displace case adds under 2 ms; numbers in the commit message.
Tests: gpu_displace.rs goldens; `just test`, `just test-gpu`, `just budget` exit 0; a vo example or vo-preview demo.

title: EG-09 Water surface simulation
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 5.

Why: water designs (rings from each word, a pool under the text) need a real wave surface with memory, which closed-form ripples cannot give. vo has no field simulation today.

Do:
- A height-field wave simulation (wave equation with damping) on a GPU grid, as a `Sim` of crates/vo-sim (EG-00): fixed 120 Hz tick, events with timestamps, snapshots, `state_at(t)`.
- Drops are events: from word onsets and voice level (the caller turns signals into recorded events; the sim never reads live audio directly), each with position, radius and strength.
- Output a height texture and a normal texture that EG-10 (shading) and EG-03 (texture displacement) can sample.
- Grid size is a parameter; default low (for example 128x64 for a 600x300 popup). Document GPU cost per tick and snapshot memory.
- Reduced motion: drops are ignored and the surface stays flat.
- Stable at any frame rate: the tick count at t depends only on t.
Files: crates/vo-sim/src/water.rs and crates/vo-sim/src/wgsl/water.wgsl (new); crates/vo-sim/tests/gpu_water.rs (new).

Acceptance:
- Given two drops 40 cells apart at t = 0 and 0.1 s, when the state is read back at t = 0.6 s, then the height midway between them shows constructive interference (larger than either single-drop run at that point, within tolerance), and the max |height| at t = 4 s is under 5 % of its peak (damping).
- Given the same events, when sampled through frame steps of 1/144 s and of 1/60 s, then the height textures at the same t are byte-identical.
- Given a seek back from t = 5 s to t = 2 s, then the state equals a fresh run to 2 s.
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1 (or the sim's reduced flag), then heights stay 0.
- Given the default grid at 600x300, then GPU time per tick plus the normal pass is under 0.3 ms (timestamp queries; skipped without them), number logged.
Tests: crates/vo-sim/tests/gpu_water.rs for the cases above (run by `just test-gpu`); `just test`, `just lint` exit 0; a vo-preview demo or vo example that shows the height field as grey, with drops from a scripted onset list.

title: EG-31 Backgrounds that know where the words are
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 17.

Why: a background cannot react to where words are. The jump-flood text field (`TextField`, crates/vo-3d/src/field.rs) exists but only vo-3d's `Stack` uses it, and vo-render cannot depend on vo-3d.

Do:
- Move `TextField` and field.wgsl into crates/vo-render/src/text_field.rs; re-export from vo-3d so its API and tests stay.
- Material inputs: `text_dist(px) -> vec4f` (signed distance in pixels, direction away from ink, coverage) through the EG-02 texture binding, and a word table (up to 64 word rects with word id and age in seconds) with `word_near(px)`.
- Built only when a material in the list asks for them (a flag on the material), at half resolution as today, and only when the text changes; zero cost otherwise.
- Reduced motion: age is treated as settled, so the lift shows without a rise.
- Demo: 23 'Breathing Grid' contours brighten and lift (shading only, materials cannot move geometry) around each new word, in material_demo.

Why: stroke-write, broken-frame and the other glyph-path effects in src/bin/osd_vo/glyph_paths.rs build outlines from one fixed text style. Ported to a look with another font, size or weight, the strokes do not sit on that look's letters. Seven look beads need this first.

Do:
- Let the glyph_paths entry points (paths_overlays, paths_broken_frame, paths_word_enter and the stroke source) take the calling look's text style: font, size, weight and line height.
- Looks that use glyph paths today pass their current style, so their output does not change.

Files: src/bin/osd_vo/glyph_paths.rs, and the call sites in the looks that already use it.

Acceptance:
- Given the looks that already use glyph paths, when `--offline` runs with their features before and after, then frames are byte-identical.
- Given a test style with a different font and size, then the sampled outline bounds match that style's shaped glyph bounds within 1 px.

Tests: a unit test for the bounds match; the before/after cmp loop logged in the commit message.

title: R2-06 Phosphor terminal: Liquid Surface, Falling Letters, Breathing Halo
description:
Why: Phosphor is a quiet terminal. Round 2 adds three small motions that the engine can already draw. Design: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/redesign2/06.png.

Do:
- Liquid Surface (R2-06-a):
  - What: the waveform is a smooth flowing wave with a few particles riding it.
  - Driver and place: RMS sets amplitude. In the waveform band, not over the text.
  - Subtle: 30 or fewer particles. Reduced: the wave line only, amplitude from RMS.
  - Uses: the existing wave element and emitter.
- Falling Letters (R2-06-b):
  - What: on word commit, faint copies of its letters fall from 12 px above into place over 250 ms with a short vertical glow trail.
  - Driver and place: word-commit; positions from `Scene::word_bounds`. Above the word; the real word is at 70 % ink or more from its first frame.
  - Subtle: copy alpha 20 % or less. Rule: only letters already recognized, never upcoming text. Reduced: no fall, ink rise only.
  - Uses: a canvas with the trail layer; no EG.
- Breathing Halo (R2-06-c):
  - What: a soft arc glow behind the lower text grows and brightens as you speak, like a slow sunrise.
  - Driver and place: smoothed RMS (release 800 ms). Behind the text.
  - Subtle: alpha at the newest line 15 % or less; settles on pause. Reduced: brightness only, no growth.
  - Uses: a gradient shape; no EG.

Files: ~/work/voxtype/src/bin/osd_vo/phosphor.rs; exhibits station/r2_06_a_liquid_surface.rs, r2_06_b_falling_letters.rs and r2_06_c_breathing_halo.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given `--theme phosphor --offline DIR --moment M` for first-word, dictation, pause and final-pass, then first-word +0.12 s shows letters mid-fall; dictation shows a large halo; pause +1 s shows it small.
- Given the same script, when `--envelope` runs, then it passes (newest line: ink 70 % or more, baseline within 3 px, no scale, rotation or blur).
- Given idle-open and recording, then the RD-02 log shows idle at 30 fps or less, CPU under 2 % of a core, GPU p95 under 1 ms at 600x300.
- Given a full dictation and a cancel, then the RD-05 exit check passes.
- Given `--station --only R2-06-a,R2-06-b,R2-06-c`, then each idea plays alone in its own tile.
- Given `--motion reduced-motion`, then the moments show each reduced form above.
- Human check: the maintainer approves a recorded clip of one dictation (`--record`, played with `--preview --replay`).

Tests: Falling copies are gone 250 ms after commit; halo radius is a pure function of RMS; no new engine code is needed. Rendering one moment twice gives identical frames.

title: EG-24 Images and app icons
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 14.

Why: the delivery receipt says 'typed into konsole' but cannot show the app's icon. There is no image element; `vo_scene::svg` reads single-colour icons into paths only.

Do:
- Image element `Element::image(key, source)` for PNG (the `png` crate) and full-colour SVG (resvg; check the licence of the version you add, recent ones are Apache-2.0 or MIT). Rasterised at logical size times surface scale; cache keyed by (file, pixel size), LRU, at most 8 MB.
- Draw: a textured quad through the EG-02 texture binding, premultiplied and sRGB-correct. CPU first frame (cpu.rs): draw it if already decoded, else skip.
- Icon lookup in the popup, off the render thread: app id (src/osd/target.rs) to `<id>.desktop` or a `StartupWMClass` match in XDG data dirs, its `Icon=`, then the icon theme (kdeglobals `[Icons] Theme`, then hicolor), scalable first. Until found, the chip shows no icon; a failed lookup is logged once at debug.
- The receipt chip (src/bin/osd_vo/lifecycle.rs) shows the icon at text height.

Files: crates/vo-scene/src/image.rs (new), crates/vo-render/src/image.rs (new), src/bin/osd_vo/app_icon.rs (new) and lifecycle.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a test PNG and SVG in tests/fixtures, then GPU goldens match at scale 1 and 1.5.
- Given app id `org.kde.konsole` and a fixture XDG tree, then lookup returns the fixture's scalable icon path; given an unknown id, None.
- Given the receipt moment (`--offline --moment` with a fixture icon dir), then the chip draws the icon (golden).
- Given 100 images of 1 MB each, then the cache stays at most 8 MB (unit test).
- `effect_cost` case `image-icon`: p95 at most 0.05 ms at 600x300, logged.
- The first frame is never delayed by the lookup.

Tests: unit tests for desktop-file and theme lookup, cache eviction, decode errors; GPU goldens above; light mode golden.

title: RD-03 Seven new look slots for the concepts with no look yet
description:
Why: concepts 01, 05, 08, 15, 19, 20 and 24 have no popup look. This bead adds the shared plumbing for all seven at once, so each new-look bead then owns only its own file.

Do:
- src/osd/config.rs: OsdTheme variants Orb, Chrome, Glass, Biolume, Aurora, Hologram, River (config names orb, chrome, glass, biolume, aurora, hologram, river; serde kebab-case and `parse_str`), each with a one-line doc comment that says the vo frontend draws it and gtk4 draws swiss. Append them to `OsdTheme::VO_LOOKS` (now 27), so the look chord cycles through them.
- src/bin/voxtype_osd.rs: add them to `vo_draws`, or the launcher starts the gtk4 frontend for them.
- src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs: dispatch each to a stub module src/bin/osd_vo/<name>.rs whose view calls the swiss view, so the stub is the plain swiss panel until its look bead lands. `Look::surface()` and placement use the swiss size for them. Update the `--theme` help text to list the vo looks.
- src/bin/osd_vo/wall.rs: concept labels for the seven (concept 01, 05, 08, 15, 19, 20, 24).
- Do not add rows to src/bin/osd_vo/defaults.rs (RD-01 ends its match with a fallback); each look's FX bead adds its row.
Files: src/osd/config.rs, src/bin/voxtype_osd.rs, src/bin/voxtype_osd_vo.rs, src/bin/osd_vo/wall.rs, src/bin/osd_vo/{orb,chrome,glass,biolume,aurora,hologram,river}.rs (new stubs).

Acceptance:
- Given `[osd] theme = "chrome"`, when the config is parsed, then theme is OsdTheme::Chrome; an unknown name still falls back as today.
- Given the launcher and theme chrome, then `vo_draws` is true.
- Given OsdTheme::VO_LOOKS, then it has 27 entries with no duplicates, and stepping the look chord 27 times from swiss (src/osd/look_step.rs) returns to swiss and visits each look once.
- Given each new look, when `voxtype-osd-vo --envelope --theme <name>` runs, then it exits 0, also with `--cancel`.
- Given `voxtype-osd-vo --wall --offline DIR` with the default theme list, then it exits 0 and the wall shows 27 cells.
Tests: config parse tests for the seven names; a look_step test for the 27-look cycle; `heavy-build cargo test --lib osd::` and `heavy-build cargo test --features osd-vo --bin voxtype-osd-vo` exit 0; the envelope runs above, with their GPU p95 logged.

title: R2-22 Mission control: Breath Ripple, Typewriter Reveal, Spectral Focus
description:
Why: Mission control is dense with panels. Round 2 adds a light swirl behind the transcript, a key-press reveal and a spectral haze at the tail. Design: /var/tmp/claude/fxlib/redesign2/22.png.

Do:
- Breath Ripple (R2-22-a):
  - What: a soft swirl of light rings grows behind the transcript box.
  - Driver and place: RMS and cadence. Behind the text; alpha at the newest line 15 % or less.
  - Reduced: still glow.
  - Uses: a material, or EG-34 drifting trails.
- Typewriter Reveal (R2-22-b):
  - What: the newest word appears with a paper patch behind it for 400 ms, lifts in 2 px and is darker for a moment before easing to normal weight.
  - Driver and place: word-commit. On the reading line within the envelope.
  - Subtle: total motion under 400 ms. Reduced: no lift, no patch.
  - Uses: EG-25, EG-28; weight and baseline channels.
- Spectral Focus (R2-22-c):
  - What live: fine spectral dust glows behind the provisional tail and fades as its words commit; the tail is sharp at 70 % ink.
  - What in replay: the haze may hide words ahead of the playhead, which clear to crisp as it reaches them.
  - Rule: no future words live and no blur on the reading line. Reduced: no dust.
  - Uses: particles; EG-35, EG-04 for replay.

Files: ~/work/voxtype/src/bin/osd_vo/mission.rs; exhibits station/r2_22_a_breath_ripple.rs, r2_22_b_typewriter_reveal.rs and r2_22_c_spectral_focus.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given `--theme mission --offline DIR --moment M` for first-word, dictation, pause and final-pass, then first-word +0.2 s shows the paper patch and lift; dictation shows dust at the tail; replay mid-sentence shows haze over words ahead.
- Given the same script, when `--envelope` runs, then it passes (newest line: ink 70 % or more, baseline within 3 px, no scale, rotation or blur).
- Given idle-open and recording, then the RD-02 log shows idle at 30 fps or less, CPU under 2 % of a core, GPU p95 under 1 ms at 600x300.
- Given a full dictation and a cancel, then the RD-05 exit check passes.
- Given `--station --only R2-22-a,R2-22-b,R2-22-c`, then each idea plays alone in its own tile.
- Given `--motion reduced-motion`, then the moments show each reduced form above.
- Human check: the maintainer approves a recorded clip of one dictation (`--record`, played with `--preview --replay`).

Tests: Live frames show no word the recogniser has not sent and no blur; lift stays within 2 px; replay haze covers only words ahead. Rendering one moment twice gives identical frames.

title: EG-28 Add the missing fonts
description:
Size: S. Gap cards: 16.

Why: designs call for faces the bundle lacks (assets/fonts/README.md lists what ships).

Do: add five subsets, each with its licence checked from the upstream repository before adding. Only SIL OFL 1.1 or Apache 2.0. Candidates (pick, check, or replace with an equal open face):
- `typewriter`: Courier Prime (OFL);
- `display-wide-italic`: a wide italic 80s display face (check Kanit or Exo 2 italics, both OFL);
- `ultra-condensed-heavy`: League Gothic or Big Shoulders Display Black (OFL);
- `script`: Great Vibes or Pinyon Script (OFL);
- `music`: Bravura or Noto Music (OFL), subset to the SMuFL noteheads, clefs, staff lines and accidentals the pitch staff uses.
Subset with assets/fonts/subset.sh (Latin list as the others; music by code point list). Add rows to the README table (asset name, file, source and version, copyright, licence) and a licence file for any non-OFL face. Register the names in `vo_scene::assets`.

- `FontRegistry::asset(name)` returns Ok for all five names (unit test).
- Each Latin face shapes "Hamburgefonstiv 0123 ÆØÅ" with no glyph id 0; the music face shapes every listed code point with no glyph id 0.
- Total added bytes at most 400 KB, logged in the commit message.
- Every new file has a README row with its licence; `grep -c` of rows equals the file count.
- A specimen golden in crates/vo-render/tests/gpu_fonts.rs shows each face.

Tests: the unit and golden tests above; `just test` and `just test-gpu` pass.

title: EG-35 Replay mode for looks that need the whole sentence
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: none (live dictation cannot know future words).

- Given `--offline` without `--replay`, then no frame ever shows a word before its time (display-list test).
- Two replays are byte-identical; `--envelope` on the replay exits 0.
- `--gpu-times` p95 at most 1 ms at 600x300, logged.

title: RD-05 Exit check: every look ends its show without the motion cap
description:

- Popup flag `--exit-check`: runs the scripted dictation of `--offline` without writing PNGs, prints `exit-check: ok <look> settled <s> s after exit` or `exit-check: FAIL <look> still moving <EXIT_MOTION_MAX> s after exit`, and exits 1 on FAIL. It honours `--cancel`, `--motion` and VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1.
- A scripted look switch: a moment `look-switch` in src/bin/osd_vo/moments.rs that steps the look chord mid-dictation (as `step_look` does), so a switch that leaves a loop running is caught. The look beads use this moment for their look-switch checks.

- Framework justfile: a recipe `osd-looks` that builds the popup (`heavy-build cargo build --release --features osd-vo --bin voxtype-osd-vo` in the fork, like the other `osd-*` recipes) and runs the script. Do not add it to `just all`: that gate must not depend on the fork.

title: EG-11 Fluid simulation core: ink and smoke with memory
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 6.

Why: ink, smoke and watercolour designs need a flow with memory: dye that curls, drifts and stays where it was pushed. vo has no fluid simulation; noise fields and curl forces on particles do not keep state.

Do:
- A stable-fluids grid on the GPU as a `Sim` of crates/vo-sim (EG-00): velocity and dye fields, semi-Lagrangian advection, a pressure solve with a fixed iteration count (so results do not depend on convergence timing), and vorticity confinement. Fixed 120 Hz tick, snapshots, `state_at(t)`.
- Impulses (pushes) and dye sources are timestamped events with position, direction, radius, colour and strength; the caller records them, the sim never reads live audio.
- Low resolution by default (for example 128x64 for a 600x300 popup); document GPU cost per tick and snapshot memory.
- Output a dye texture (and velocity, for EG-12 smears) that other passes can sample.
- Reduced motion: impulses are ignored; dye sources place still dye.
Files: crates/vo-sim/src/fluid.rs and crates/vo-sim/src/wgsl/fluid.wgsl (new); crates/vo-sim/tests/gpu_fluid.rs (new).

Acceptance:
- Given dye injected at one point with one sideways push at t = 0, when read back at t = 2 s, then the dye centre of mass has moved in the push direction by at least 10 cells and the dye shows curl (vorticity magnitude above a documented threshold).
- Given closed boundaries and no sources after t = 0, then total dye at t = 3 s is within 5 % of total dye at t = 0.1 s.
- Given the same events, when sampled through frame steps of 1/144 s and of 1/60 s, then dye textures at equal t are byte-identical; a seek back from 5 s to 2 s equals a fresh run to 2 s.
- Given VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1, then dye does not move after it lands.
- Given the default grid at 600x300, then GPU time per tick is under 0.4 ms (timestamp queries; skipped without them), number logged.

title: EG-23 Smooth variable-font axes
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 13.

Why: breathing type uses Roboto Flex instances quantised to steps (`Axes::quantized`: 20 weight, 1 width, 1 degree slant), so a slow loudness ramp jumps.

Do: keep the quantised instances (the font registry never drops fonts) and make the rest continuous on top of the nearest one:
- weight: the remainder becomes glyph edge dilation (`GlyphFx::weight`), calibrated per face so one step of 20 equals the dilation that matches the next instance's ink;
- width: the remainder becomes a horizontal scale in the per-glyph transform (EG-15);
- slant: the remainder becomes skew in the per-glyph transform (EG-15).
- Calibrate once per face at load (measure ink of two neighbouring instances) and cache.
- Reduced motion: unchanged from today.

Files: crates/vo-scene/src/motion/var_axes.rs, crates/vo-scene/src/flow.rs (where word channels apply), crates/vo-scene/tests/variable_font.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a weight ramp 400 to 600 over 4 s at 60 fps, then the word's ink area per frame (GPU readback) never drops and its largest frame step is at most 1.5x the median step.
- Given a width ramp 95 to 105, then the word width (layout units) never drops and its largest step is at most 1.5x the median.
- Given those ramps, then at most 11 instances are created (no extra memory).
- A reading-line ramp passes `check_scenario` (tracking within 5 %).
- `effect_cost` case `flex-breathing` adds at most 0.05 ms p95 at 600x300, logged.

Tests: unit tests for remainder maths and calibration; the two ramp tests in a GPU test; a recorded demo in text_flow_demo.

title: EG-16 Per-letter motions: tumbling arrivals, leaning digits, italic arrival, text on a wave
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 8.

Why: designs want letters that tumble in, digits that lean with pace, words that arrive slanted, and older lines on a wave. EG-15 gives per-glyph transforms.

Do: new `crates/vo-scene/src/motion/letter_motion.rs`, four closed-form motions, pure in t and the word's arrival time, selectable on live text in flow.rs:
- Tumble (01 'Magnetic Type'): a decoration copy of each new letter (word id `NO_WORD`, so the envelope ignores it) flies in from up to 40 px turning up to 360 degrees and lands within 350 ms. The real glyph stands in place at ink 0.7 or more from its first frame, rising to 1 as the copy lands.
- Lean (03): digits of a counter label (not live text) skew up to 12 degrees with words per minute and spring back in pauses.
- Italic arrival (11): a new word arrives with skew up to 5 degrees and straightens in 200 ms.
- Wave (19): glyphs of older lines (never the newest) ride y = A sin(kx - wt), A at most 3 px, turned to follow the slope.
- Reduced motion: no copy (tumble), no lean, straight arrival, still lines.
- Popup: one station exhibit per motion in src/bin/osd_vo/station/, names `letter-tumble`, `digit-lean`, `italic-arrival`, `line-wave`, reachable with `--motion`.

Files: crates/vo-scene/src/motion/letter_motion.rs (new), crates/vo-scene/src/flow.rs, src/bin/osd_vo/station/ (new exhibit file).

Acceptance:
- `voxtype-osd-vo --envelope --motion <name>` exits 0 for each of the four.
- Given a tumble arrival at time a, then at a the real glyph's ink is at least 0.7, and at a + 0.35 s the copy is gone.
- Given the wave, then every newest-line glyph has identity `xform` at all sampled t.
- Two `--offline` renders of one exhibit are byte-identical.
- `--offline --gpu-times` p95 at most 1 ms at 600x300 per motion, logged.

title: EG-33 Many tilted panes in one draw
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 19.

Why: each perspective-turned layer (`Element::rotate_x/rotate_y`, a `Warp` per layer from crates/vo-scene/src/stage.rs) costs an offscreen texture and a warp pass. 20 receding word frames cost 20 of them.

Do:
- In renderer.rs, a turned layer that holds only shapes and glyphs (no bloom, trail, mask, nested offscreen or GPU item) is drawn directly: its instances get the layer's homography in the vertex shader, with perspective-correct local coordinates for the SDF and Slug maths. Other turned layers keep the offscreen path.
- Edge anti-aliasing from screen-space derivatives, so edges stay sharp under the tilt.
- Stateless: nothing to replay.
- Demo: 20 receding word frames, in stage_demo.

- Given the same scene through both paths, then images match: mean difference at most 1/255, max at most 16/255 (edges).
- Given a turned layer with bloom, then it still goes offscreen (frame_report).
- `effect_cost` case `panes-20`: p95 at most 0.4 ms at 600x300, logged. No timestamps: skipped and said so.

title: EG-13 Ribbons and cloth that twist and fold
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 7.

Why: several designs want a silk ribbon or cloth strip that twists to show its back and swells with the voice. vo-3d meshes are rigid and uploaded once (mesh.rs); `vo_scene::ribbon` is flat 2D strands.

Do:
- New `crates/vo-3d/src/ribbon3d.rs`: a strip of N segments (default 96) along a 3D centre curve. Closed form, a pure function of t and a level history (`vo_scene::emitter::LevelTrack`): twist and folds are sums of travelling sines, width swells with level. No verlet and no state. Cloth is the same strip made wide; no collisions.
- mesh.rs: add a `uv` attribute to `Vertex` (zero in the existing builders) and `Renderer3d::update_mesh` that rewrites a mesh's vertices each frame (same count, `queue.write_buffer`).
- wgsl/mesh.wgsl: two-sided shading (front and back colour by `front_facing`), fine fibre lines along the length from uv, no culling for ribbons.
- Reduced motion: the rest pose; level changes brightness only.
- Demo `crates/vo-3d/examples/ribbon_demo.rs` with a contact sheet and `--bench`, like hero_demo.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/ribbon3d.rs (new), crates/vo-3d/src/mesh.rs, crates/vo-3d/src/wgsl/mesh.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Given twist amplitude 180 degrees, when rendered at the pose where it passes 90 degrees, then back-colour pixels are at least 10 % of ribbon pixels.
- Given level 0 and level 1, then mean strip width at level 1 is at least 1.3x (CPU test on vertices).
- Given t sampled after a forward run and after a random-order run, then the vertices are bit-identical.
- `ribbon_demo --bench` at 600x300: p95 GPU time of one ribbon at most 0.3 ms, logged in the commit message. Without timestamp queries it prints that and exits 0.
- `just test-gpu` passes; existing vo-3d goldens unchanged.

Tests: unit tests for width, twist, purity; GPU goldens (crates/vo-3d/tests/goldens) at scale 1 and 1.5, a light background, and reduced motion. The CPU first frame (vo-render cpu.rs) skips GPU items: assert the demo's first CPU frame does not panic.

title: EG-17 3D reflections from a scene, not a fixed studio
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 9, 10.

Why: the chrome hero reflects a fixed studio gradient (`HeroLook::Chrome { top, bottom, light }` in sdf.rs). It should reflect the popup itself, which is how chrome can seem to reflect its surroundings without screen capture.

Do:
- New `crates/vo-3d/src/env.rs`: an environment texture (256x128, Rgba16Float, equirectangular). Front half: a low-resolution capture (128x64) of the popup's own layers under the hero through EG-01. The rest: a procedural sky gradient. Rebuild at most 30 times a second and only when the capture changed.
- `HeroLook::Chrome` gets `env: Option<Env>`; sdf_hero.wgsl looks up the reflected ray in it. `None` keeps today's studio exactly.
- No screen pixels: only the popup's own layers.
- Reduced motion: no change needed (a reflection is not motion); say so in the doc comment.
- Extend hero_demo with a chrome blob over a panel and a waveform.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/env.rs (new), crates/vo-3d/src/sdf.rs, crates/vo-3d/src/wgsl/sdf_hero.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Given `env: None`, then the gpu_hero goldens are unchanged.
- Given a red bar below and left of the blob, then the mean red of the blob's lower-left quarter exceeds its upper-right quarter by at least 0.1 (linear).
- Given an unchanged backdrop for 30 frames, then the env texture is rebuilt once (counter).
- `hero_demo --bench` at 600x300: chrome with env adds at most 0.1 ms p95 over chrome without, logged. No timestamps: print and exit 0.
- Env memory is 256 KB (logged).

Tests: unit tests for the direction-to-texel mapping; GPU goldens at scale 1 and 1.5 and light mode; a same-t-same-bytes determinism test.

title: RD-02 Living idle motion: policy, frame pacing and a CPU budget per look
description:
Why: the maintainer wants every look to feel alive with small idle animations while the popup is open. Motion rule 8 (settle to still) and the budget gate (0 idle frames) forbid that today. This bead sets the new rule and the tools that hold it, before any look adds idle motion.

Do:
- Fix the policy with a short Fable consult (consult-oracles skill). Starting proposal: idle loops run at most at `vo_core::ambient::AMBIENT_FPS` (30 fps) through `Element::ambient(LoopProp, Loop)` and the paced wakes in crates/vo/src/live.rs; only while the popup is open; never on the newest (reading) line; left out under reduced motion (`reduced-motion` or VO_REDUCED_MOTION=1); not drawn by the CPU first frame (the first frame shows the rest pose); dropped from the view as soon as the app asks to exit, so the show settles well inside EXIT_MOTION_MAX (3 s).
- Add a vo helper only if the ambient path cannot serve the idle ideas in docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 4 (for example a paced shader time for a material).
- Per-look measurement, new script scripts/osd-vo-budget.sh in ~/work/voxtype: for each look in OsdTheme::VO_LOOKS with its defaults, CPU time per second of the popup process (from /proc/<pid>/stat) live in a nested `kwin_wayland --virtual` (for example `--wall --wall-themes <look> --wall-cols 1 --wall-size 600x300 --wall-script demo`, or a small dev flag if that is not representative), split into recording and idle-open; GPU p95 per frame from `--offline --gpu-times` on the `dictation` and `long-silence` moments. Write /var/tmp/claude/vo-budget/looks.tsv (look, state, cpu_pct, frames_per_s, gpu_ms_p95). Exit 1 naming the look when a limit is crossed. Limits are env vars, defaults from the consult; proposal: idle-open under 2 % of one core and at most 30 frames per second, GPU under 1 ms p95 at 600x300; the recording CPU limit is set from today's measurement.
- Framework scripts/budget.sh: keep `VO_BUDGET_IDLE_FRAMES=0` for the toast; add a live run of an example that keeps one ambient loop running while idle (ambient_demo or a new one) whose idle frames must stay at or under 30 per second.
- Put today's CPU per look during a replayed dictation (the maintainer asked for it) in docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md, and the decided policy and limits in docs/MOTION-PLAN.md rule 8 and REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 4.
Files: ~/work/voxtype/scripts/osd-vo-budget.sh (new), ~/work/voxtype-osd-gpu/scripts/budget.sh, docs/MOTION-PLAN.md, docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md; crates/vo only if a helper is needed.

Acceptance:
- Given the toast, when `just budget` runs, then it exits 0 with 0 idle frames as today.
- Given that example idle in a nested KWin for 10 s, then `just budget` counts at most 300 frames and passes.
- Given every look with its defaults, when scripts/osd-vo-budget.sh runs, then looks.tsv has two rows per look, and the script exits 1 exactly when a row is over its limit (proved once with a limit forced to 0). Looks over a limit today are listed in docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md for their look beads.
- Given an ambient loop and an exit at t, then a vo unit test shows the scene stops moving before t + EXIT_MOTION_MAX (no "still moving" path).
Tests: the vo unit test above; both scripts run once, numbers pasted into docs/REDESIGN-PLAN.md and the commit message.

Decided (lead): a caret that blinks or breathes in its own box on the reading line is allowed (type, palette, phosphor). The newest line's glyphs never move, scale, blur or lose ink.

title: EG-22 Shapes that bulge and melt together
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 12.

Why: SDF shapes are drawn one at a time. Designs want a capsule that swells around one word, a panel edge that ripples, and blobs that melt together (the canvas `blob` covers only two circles).

Do:
- Shape groups: a new shape kind in shapes.wgsl that combines up to 8 primitives (rounded rect, circle, capsule) by smooth union with radius k. Primitives live in a storage buffer; the instance holds its range. Glow, shadow and stroke paints use the combined distance.
- Bulge: a group member placed on a capsule (centre, width, height). Edge ripple: an offset A sin(...) along the edge, A at most 2 px.
- API: a group variant in `vo_scene::display` and `Painter::shape_group` in canvas.rs; motion comes from the canvas (pure in t).
- cpu.rs (CPU first frame) runs the same maths.
- Reduced motion: settled bulge size, no ripple.
- Demo: the 03 capsule bulging around the spoken word, as a station exhibit `capsule-bulge` or a vo example.

Files: crates/vo-render/src/wgsl/shapes.wgsl, crates/vo-render/src/shapes.rs, crates/vo-scene/src/display.rs, crates/vo-render/src/cpu.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given a group with one primitive, then it renders identical to the plain shape (golden equality).
- Given two touching circles with k = 10, then coverage at the joint is 1 (no seam).
- Given the CPU path, then it matches the GPU within the existing CPU tolerance.
- `effect_cost` case `shape-group-8`: p95 at most 0.1 ms at 600x300, logged. No timestamps: skipped and said so.

title: RD-04 Letters stay faint in a word that grows while it fades in
description:
Why: known open bug. When a live word grows (more letters arrive in a later preview) while it is still fading in, the new letters can stay faint. Seen on dotmatrix, tron and radial. Faint letters on the newest line also break the reading-line envelope (ink at least 70 % from the first frame).

Do:
- Reproduce first: a vo-scene unit test that feeds a live-text word "hel" at t=0 with a fade-in enter, then "hello" at t=0.05 (inside the fade), and samples each glyph's ink at the end of the fade.
- Find and fix the cause in the framework's live-text word state. Start at crates/vo-scene/src/flow.rs (the glyph diff near `T08, T09`, and word enter) and crates/vo-scene/src/arrival.rs (`Arrival::Readable`, INK = 0.7). New letters of a growing word must join the word's fade at its current progress or start at full readable ink, never restart at 0 or freeze.
- Remove any look-side workaround in the popup for this bug, if one exists (search dotmatrix.rs, tron.rs, radial.rs).

- Given the same word with the default `Arrival::Readable`, at every sample from its first frame, then every glyph's ink is at least arrival::INK (0.7).

title: EG-04 Layer blur and frosted shapes
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 11.

Why: vo has no blur of a layer or of what is under a shape; only glyph edge softening, bloom and motion blur. Depth-stack sheets, out-of-focus far words and soft reflections need a real blur.

Do:
- Layer blur: a separable blur (dual Kawase or two-pass Gaussian, the implementer picks by measured cost) on an offscreen layer, with an animatable radius (a new animatable property on layers; pick a name that does not clash with the text-effect blur).
- Frost on shapes: a shape option that blurs its backdrop (EG-01) inside the shape's outline, so a sheet frosts the lines behind it.
- Radius 0 costs nothing (no pass). The radius follows the quality tier (`vo_render::Quality`, VO_QUALITY): `minimal` draws no blur.
- Reduced motion: the radius does not animate (it jumps to its target).
- Never on the newest (reading) line: the envelope forbids blur there; frost behind it is fine.
- Add effect_cost cases `layer blur r8` and `frost r8`.

- Given radius 0, then output equals the unblurred layer byte for byte, and effect_cost shows no added pass.
- Given effect_cost at 600x300, then each blur case adds under 2 ms, and the depth-stack demo stays under 1 ms p95 for the whole frame; numbers in the commit message.
- Given the same scene at the same t twice, then frames are byte-identical.
Tests: gpu_blur.rs goldens and the impulse test; `just test`, `just test-gpu`, `just budget` exit 0; a vo-preview demo of frosted sheets.

title: EG-07 Frosted glass looks use KDE blur-behind, shaped to the outline
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 1, 10.

Why: frosted glass looks need the desktop blurred behind them, and the maintainer chose compositor blur over screen capture. vo can already ask KWin to blur (ext-background-effect, crates/vo-host-wayland/src/blur.rs), and `DisplayList::blur_region` (crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs) already steps rounded corners. But only axis-aligned rounded-rect glass gets a region, rotated glass gets its bounding box, and the popup never turns blur on.

Do:
- Blur region from any outline: chamfers, notches, filled paths and the shapes EG-06 gives glass, and rotated or tilted layers. Step the region per row of physical pixels along slanted and curved edges, as `blur_rects` does for corners, so no blur spills past the outline. Cap the rect count (for example 256) by merging rows; document the cap.
- A non-glass translucent element can also ask for blur behind its outline.
- When the compositor has no blur (`caps.backdrop_blur` false), the look draws its plain tint and logs once.
- One popup helper in ~/work/voxtype src/bin/osd_vo/kit.rs that a look calls to turn blur-behind on for its panel outline. Do not edit look files: each look adopts it in its own look or R2 bead.
Files: crates/vo-scene/src/glass.rs (region from outlines), crates/vo-host-wayland/src/blur.rs (only if the region path needs it); src/bin/osd_vo/kit.rs in the popup.

Acceptance:
- Given a chamfered octagon (chamfer 12 px) at scale 1 and 1.25, then a unit test shows every region rect lies inside the outline (no spill beyond 1 physical px) and the rects cover at least 97 % of its area, with at most the documented rect count.
- Given a card rotated 15 degrees, then the same two checks hold.
- Given a rounded rect, then the region equals today's `blur_rects` output.
- Given a nested `kwin_wayland --virtual` with a sharp checkerboard behind a demo surface with an octagon glass (a vo example, or `blur_probe` extended), when a screenshot is taken (spectacle needs KWIN_WAYLAND_NO_PERMISSION_CHECKS=1), then pixels outside the outline equal the checkerboard, and pixel variance inside is at most half of outside.
- Given a compositor without blur, then the demo draws and logs "no compositor blur" once.
Tests: the unit tests in crates/vo-scene; the nested KWin screenshot check as a script or test with its numbers logged; `just test` and `just lint` exit 0; the kit.rs helper unit-tested for its region on the swiss panel.

title: EG-27 Particles drawn as tiny letters
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 15.

Why: glyph dust and letters streaming out of an orb need each particle drawn as a small turned letter. Sprites today are soft, dot, bokeh or spark (`SpriteStyle` in emitter.rs).

Do:
- `SpriteStyle::Glyph { font, chars, size }`: each particle shows one glyph from `chars`, picked by a hash of its index; its turn comes from velocity or a spin rate.
- Draw: a compute pass writes one Slug glyph instance per live particle (using EG-15's transform in `lin`) into a storage buffer and the Slug pipeline draws it with an indirect draw. The glyphs are Slug-encoded when the emitter is made. At most 4096 glyph particles per emitter.
- Light mode (`Renderer::set_light`): normal blend instead of additive, so letters stay visible on light backgrounds.
- Reduced motion: letters fade in place, no travel.
- CPU first frame: skipped, as other emitters.
- Demo: letters streaming from an orb in crates/vo/examples/particles_v2.rs.

Acceptance:
- Given one glyph particle at rest and unturned, then its pixels equal the same glyph drawn as text, mean difference at most 2/255.
- Given 2000 glyph particles at 10 px, then p95 is at most 0.4 ms at 600x300 (`effect_cost` or particles_bench case), logged. No timestamps: skipped and said so.
- Given a seek back, then the frame equals a fresh run (bytes).
- Given light mode, then the letters' mean luminance differs from the light background by at least 0.3.

Tests: unit tests for glyph pick and limits; GPU goldens at scale 1 and 1.5 and light mode.

title: EG-14 Text on curved surfaces
description:
Size: L. Gap cards: 7.

Why: 'Breathing Scroll' (20) and 'Page Reveal' (08) print words on a strip that curls or a page that turns. vo-3d meshes have no textures.

Do:
- Draw a text display list into a texture with the normal 2D renderer, the way `field.rs` already does (no backdrop capture needed). Texel density: one texel per device pixel at the nearest point, capped at 2x the surface scale and 2048 px. Redraw only when the text, size or scale changes.
- Textured meshes in vo-3d: a draw may bind one premultiplied texture, sampled by `uv` (EG-13 adds it) with linear filtering and mipmaps. Untextured meshes keep today's pipeline.
- Two closed-form shapes: a scroll (an EG-13 strip rolled on a cylinder, `unroll` 0 to 1) and a page turn (a plane bent around a moving cylinder axis, `turn` 0 to 1).
- Older lines, titles and final text only: the reading line never goes on a curved surface (say so in the doc comment).
- Reduced motion: flat page, the unroll or turn jumps to its end.
- Demo `crates/vo-3d/examples/surface_text_demo.rs` with a contact sheet and `--bench`.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/surface_text.rs (new), crates/vo-3d/src/render.rs (textured pipeline), crates/vo-3d/src/wgsl/mesh.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Given a flat page (turn 0) with 24 px text, then it matches the same text drawn by the 2D renderer: mean difference at most 2/255.
- Given scale 1.5, then the text texture is 1.5x the size at scale 1 (unit test).
- Given text unchanged for 60 frames, then the texture is drawn once (counter).
- `surface_text_demo --bench` at 600x300: p95 at most 0.4 ms for a 600x120 page; texture memory printed and at most 3 MB. Both logged in the commit message. No timestamps: print and exit 0.

Tests: unit tests for texel size and the page and scroll maths; GPU goldens of the scroll at unroll 0.5 and the page at turn 0.5, at scale 1 and 1.5, plus light background and reduced motion; a determinism test (same t, same bytes).

title: EG-18 Soft shadows in 3D
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 9.

Why: typebars, platens and other meshes float without contact shadows. vo-3d has one key light and no shadows.

Do:
- New `crates/vo-3d/src/shadow.rs`: a shadow map for the directional key light, 512x512 Depth16 by default (512 KB), fit to the meshes' bounds each frame. Soft edges by PCF (Poisson disc, 8 to 16 taps) with a `softness` setting in pixels.
- `Frame3d` gets `shadows: Option<Shadows { softness, size }>`. `None` draws exactly as today.
- Casters: meshes. Receivers: the floor (floor.wgsl) and meshes (mesh.wgsl). The raymarched hero neither casts nor receives (out of scope).
- Stateless: rebuilt from the current pose each frame, so replay is exact.
- Demo `crates/vo-3d/examples/shadow_demo.rs`: a box and a torus over the floor, contact sheet and `--bench`.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/shadow.rs (new), crates/vo-3d/src/render.rs, crates/vo-3d/src/wgsl/mesh.wgsl and floor.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Given `shadows: None`, then every existing vo-3d golden is unchanged.
- Given a box 40 px above the floor, then the floor under it is at least 30 % darker than open floor, and the edge goes from 10 % to 90 % of that darkening over at least 3 px (scanline check).
- `shadow_demo --bench` at 600x300: shadows add at most 0.25 ms p95, logged in the commit message. No timestamps: print and exit 0.

Tests: unit test for the light-space fit (all casters inside the map); GPU goldens at scale 1 and 1.5 and on a light floor; a test that `None` creates no shadow texture.

title: EG-29 Pen-stroke order for the real UI font
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 16.

Why: stroke writing (crates/vo-scene/src/stroke_write.rs) draws Hershey Script Simplex pen strokes over the real glyph, so the hand does not match the face that settles.

Do:
- New `crates/vo-scene/src/centreline.rs`: rasterise the glyph outline (`path::glyph_path`) to a 96 px grid with a small scanline fill (no new dependency), thin it (Zhang-Suen), trace the skeleton into polylines, smooth them, and order strokes: top before bottom, left before right, horizontal before vertical at a crossing, each drawn left to right or top to bottom.
- Cache per (font, glyph). Computed lazily, never on the frame that first shows the word: precompute on a worker or reuse the outline-trace fallback for that frame.
- `Writing::new` gets a stroke source: `Hershey` (today, the default) or `Font` (centrelines). Looks switch in their own beads.
- The ink floor (0.7 on the reading line) is unchanged.

Files: crates/vo-scene/src/centreline.rs (new), crates/vo-scene/src/stroke_write.rs.

Acceptance:
- For every ASCII letter and digit in `extra-condensed-bold` (Saira) and `grotesk` (Inter): the centrelines stroked at the glyph's stem width cover at least 95 % of the glyph's ink, with at most 5 % of the stroke outside it (CPU raster test).
- Stroke counts: o = 1, l = 1, T = 2, H = 3; T's horizontal comes first.
- Same input, same output (bit-identical).
- All 95 ASCII glyphs of one face in at most 50 ms in release, logged.
- Existing stroke_write tests and goldens pass with the `Hershey` default.
- `check_scenario` passes for a demo with the `Font` source.

Tests: unit tests above in crates/vo-scene/tests/centreline.rs; a GPU golden of a word half written at scale 1 and 1.5.

title: EG-12 Ink and smoke looks from the fluid
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 6.

Why: the EG-11 fluid is only a field until words drive it and it is drawn. Concepts 19 ("Luminous Ink") and 15 ("Ink Reveal") need ink that blooms where words land and smoke that follows the voice.

- Fresh glyphs of older lines may smear along the flow through EG-03's texture displacement, fed by the velocity texture. The newest (reading) line is never displaced.

title: EG-26 Particles form any shape: wire up points and mask forces
description:
Size: S. Gap cards: 15.

Why: `Particles::set_points` (`PointForm`) and `Particles::set_mask` (`MaskField`) in crates/vo-render/src/particles.rs exist but only tests call them. Scenes cannot make particles form a check mark or an icon, or keep them inside text.

Do:

- `EmitterSource::text_mask(...)` builds a `MaskField` from text coverage for the existing mask force.
- particle_layer.rs applies target and mask changes at their recorded times, as it does for particle words, so a seek replays them.

- Given a seek back to an earlier t, then the frame equals a fresh run to that t (bytes).

  - What: a droplet from the mic falls into a water strip under the text; each word sends one ring.

title: EG-20 3D can pass in front of text (except the reading line)
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 9.

Why: 3D is drawn either all behind or all over the text. 'Orbiting Words' (20) needs a ring that passes behind the text and then in front of older lines, while the reading line always stays on top.

Do:
- crates/vo-3d/src/item.rs: an item can be drawn as two halves split at the text plane (z = 0 in stage space): `Part::Behind` and `Part::Front`, by a clip on view-space z in the 3D pass. One `Source3d`, drawn twice.
- Scene: `Element::gpu_split(key, source)` (or a flag on `Element::gpu`) puts the back half where the element sits and the front half after the live text.
- The front half is cut out inside the newest line's ink rectangles, padded by 4 px. The rectangles come from the display list (glyphs with word ids on the last row). The reading line is never covered.
- crates/vo-3d/src/stack.rs (the fixed-order path) keeps its order; say so in its docs.
- Reduced motion: the demo's orbit stands still.
- Demo `crates/vo-3d/examples/orbit_words_demo.rs`, contact sheet and `--bench`.

Files: crates/vo-3d/src/item.rs, crates/vo-3d/src/render.rs (clip uniform), crates/vo-scene/src/gpu.rs (split flag and line rectangles).

Acceptance:
- Given a ring crossing three lines, then (a) where the front half crosses an older line, the pixels differ from a render without the ring; (b) where the back half crosses, text pixels with coverage 0.9 or more equal the no-ring render; (c) every pixel inside the newest line's padded rectangles equals the render without the front half, exactly.
- `check_scenario` on the demo reports no breach.
- `--bench` at 600x300: both halves cost at most 1.3x the single item, logged. No timestamps: print and exit 0.
- Same t gives the same bytes.

Tests: unit test for the rectangle list; GPU goldens at scale 1 and 1.5 and light mode for (a) to (c).

title: EG-25 Paper, fabric and grain textures
description:
Size: S. Gap cards: 14.

Why: typewriter paper, woven ribbon, rubber and film grain look flat with today's procedural noise.

- Film grain changes 24 times a second: offset from a hash of floor(t x 24), pure in t. Reduced motion: grain still.
- CPU first frame: the panel's base colour.
- Demo: paper and ribbon panels in material_demo.

Files: crates/vo/examples/make_textures.rs (new), assets/textures/ (new), crates/vo-scene/src/material.rs, crates/vo-render/src/wgsl/materials.wgsl.

Acceptance:
- Running the generator again gives byte-identical tiles.
- Each tile wraps: the mean difference between its first and last column (and row) is at most 1.5x the mean difference between neighbouring interior columns.
- Given film grain at t and t + 0.01 s, then identical frames; at t and t + 1/24 s, different.
- `effect_cost` case `paper-panel`: p95 at most 0.05 ms at 600x300, logged. Added binary size (256 KB) logged.

title: EG-00 vo-sim crate: fixed-tick simulations that replay
description:
Size: S. Why: the water (EG-09) and fluid (EG-11) simulations need the same base: a grid that steps at a fixed tick and can be rebuilt at any time t. One bead makes the crate, so the two lanes do not both create it.

Do:
- New crate crates/vo-sim (the workspace takes crates/* already; add it to `just all` only if a recipe needs it). A small `Sim` trait: fixed tick (120 Hz, like the particles), seeded events with timestamps (drops, pushes, dye), `step`, `snapshot`, `restore`, and `state_at(t)` that restores the nearest snapshot at or before t and steps forward. Follow the seek pattern of crates/vo-render/src/particles.rs (`Particles::snapshot`).
- Events between ticks apply at the first tick at or after their time, so the state at t depends only on t and the event list, never on how often frames were drawn.
- Snapshot policy: one every N ticks (default 1 s), with a memory cap; document both and the cost of a seek.
- A reference sim: a dot of value that diffuses on a small grid (for example 64x32). It may run on the CPU so its tests run in `just test`; the trait must not assume the CPU, since EG-09 and EG-11 run on the GPU.
Files: crates/vo-sim/Cargo.toml, crates/vo-sim/src/lib.rs, crates/vo-sim/src/snapshot.rs, crates/vo-sim/src/reference.rs (all new).

Acceptance:
- Given the reference sim with three timed events, when it is sampled at the same t through frame steps of 1/144 s and of 1/60 s, then the two states are byte-identical.
- Given a run to t = 5 s and a seek back to t = 2.3 s, then the state equals a fresh run to 2.3 s, byte for byte.
- Given an event at t = 1.004 s, then it applies at tick 121 (the first tick at or after it) in both frame schedules.
- Given 60 s of run time, then snapshot memory stays under the documented cap.
- Given `just test` and `just lint`, then both exit 0.
Tests: unit tests for the four cases above in crates/vo-sim; log seek time from 0 to 60 s in the test output.

title: EG-06 Glass on any outline and on tilted layers
description:
Size: M. Gap cards: 4, 12.

Why: glass works only on axis-aligned rounded rects (`GlassDraw` in crates/vo-render/src/glass.rs says rotation is not supported). The designs need glass chamfers, prisms, bells and wavy edges, and glass cards on tilted layers.

- Glass follows rotated and perspective-tilted layers: rim and sheen follow the warped quad, not its bounding box.
- Scope: drawing only. The compositor blur region for these outlines is EG-07; here, a non-rect or rotated glass keeps today's bounding-box blur region.
- Light and dark presets both work on the new outlines, and text over them passes the AX01 contrast check (`Glass::contrast`).
- Reduced motion: the orbiting rim head and sheen sweep stop as they do today on rects.
